notes: Perfect match (Jaccard=1.0) on mutational spectrum findings. Both agree the differential distribution of transitions vs transversions and REV1/UNG genetic evidence are well-supported. Peer review notes REV1 could have pleiotropic effects but accepts findings.

Near-perfect match (Jaccard=0.923) on yeast kataegis recapitulation. Both strongly support the experimental demonstration. LLM includes C29 (strand polarity) in this group; peer review separates it but still supports it (see R2 peer).
Strong match (Jaccard=0.917) on UNG-dependence of kataegis. Both praise this as key mechanistic insight. LLM includes C39 which peer review doesn't explicitly address, but overall agreement is clear.

Good overlap (Jaccard=0.8) on mechanistic model of break-repair and ssDNA exposure. LLM supports the end resection interpretation, but peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting ssDNA could arise from chromatin breathing rather than long resection zones. Key interpretive disagreement.

Moderate match (Jaccard=0.5) on I-SceI break nucleation of kataegis. Both support the finding. LLM includes C73, C102, C103 not in peer review group; peer review suggests adding controls but accepts the result.

Partial overlap (Jaccard=0.333) on APOBEC3B/A identification. Both support the signature matching and implication in breast cancer. LLM groups C53, C54 with this result; peer review doesn't explicitly address these but accepts overall conclusion.

Moderate match (Jaccard=0.429) on sequence context preferences for AID, APOBEC3C, APOBEC3G. Both support these findings. Peer review asks about protein equivalence (methodological question) but doesn't challenge the sequence preference data.

Partial match (Jaccard=0.4) on functional validation in mammalian cells. Both support DNA damage findings (C69, C70). LLM includes C68 (cell viability) not explicitly in peer review group, but overall agreement on functional validation.

Partial match (Jaccard=0.4) on APOBEC3B expression in breast cancer. Both support expression data (C71, C95). LLM includes C72 and groups separately from functional validation; peer review implicitly accepts both together.
Low overlap (Jaccard=0.2) but semantic agreement on overall implication of APOBEC3B/A in breast cancer hypermutation (C7, C97). Both support this main conclusion through converging evidence.

Minimal overlap (Jaccard=0.077) on strand polarity (C29). LLM groups this with broader kataegis recapitulation; peer review separates it but still supports, requesting only clarification of terminology.

Partial overlap (Jaccard=0.308) on sequence context for APOBEC3A/B (C60-C63). Both support the refined sequence preferences. LLM emphasizes novel detailed preferences; peer review accepts within broader APOBEC3B/A identification.
